unit.title: Subjunctive: impersonal expressions
unit.subtitle: It's important that…: es importante que, es necesario que, es mejor que

grammar.title: Es + adjective + que: judging, advising, guessing
grammar.intro: One of the most useful subjunctive patterns is es + [adjective] + que. When you judge, advise, or state something is possible — important, necessary, better, likely — the verb after que flips to the subjunctive. But watch the twist at the end: expressions of plain fact keep the indicative.

sections.heading: The pattern
sections.body: Start with es + an adjective of value or possibility, add que, then a subjunctive verb. It works for anyone — that's why it's called impersonal.

sections.heading: A natural way to advise
sections.body: These expressions are how Spanish gives soft advice. Es mejor que and hace falta que let you suggest without ordering. Notice the irregulars slip right in:

ex.en: It's necessary that you go to the doctor.

sections.heading: The exception: facts keep the indicative
sections.body: Not every es… que takes the subjunctive. When the expression states a plain fact — es verdad que, es evidente que, es cierto que — the verb stays in the indicative.

ex.en: It's true that you work a lot.
It's obvious you know the answer.

takeaways: Es + [value/possibility] + que → subjunctive: es importante que estudies.
Triggers: es importante/necesario/posible/mejor que, hace falta que.
Irregulars fit right in: vayas, hagas, sepas, esté, tenga.
Facts keep the indicative: es verdad/evidente/cierto que trabajas.

mistakes.why: A value judgment + que takes the subjunctive: estudies, not estudias.

mistakes.w: Es necesario que vas al médico.
mistakes.r: Es necesario que vayas al médico.
mistakes.why: ir flips to the subjunctive here: vayas, not vas.
Es verdad que states a fact, so keep the indicative: estudias.

exercises.prompt_en: It's important that you study more.

exercises.prompt: Es verdad que Madrid ___ muy grande.
exercises.prompt_en: It's true that Madrid is very big.
exercises.no: Es verdad que states a fact → indicative: “es”.
“Es mejor que descanses” — descansar flips to descanses.

exercises.prompt: Es necesario que tú ___ a tiempo. (llegar)
exercises.prompt_en: It's necessary that you arrive on time.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Es necesario que llegues a tiempo.

exercises.prompt: Match each infinitive to its subjunctive (tú) form.

exercises.translation: It's possible it will rain tomorrow.
exercises.no: It was: “Es posible que llueva mañana.” (It's possible it will rain tomorrow.)

exercises.scenario: A friend is exhausted before work 😴

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.es: Estoy muy cansado y mañana trabajo.
lines.en: I'm very tired and I work tomorrow.

exercises.no: After 'es mejor que' use the subjunctive: “Es mejor que descanses.” (It's better that you rest.)
